# Supadomain

> Supadomain is a self-hosted domain expiration monitor (Nuxt 4, MongoDB). It reads expiry dates over RDAP when a domain is added or refreshed, compares them with alert thresholds every hour and posts Slack alerts. This site also has a free in-browser domain expiry checker.

## Docs

- [Home](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/): what Supadomain does and its limits
- [Getting started](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/guide/getting-started): install on Node.js and MongoDB
- [How to monitor domain expiration](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/guide/monitor-domain-expiration): manual checks and monitors compared
- [Slack expiry alerts](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/guide/slack-alerts): webhook setup and when an alert fires
- [RDAP vs WHOIS](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/guide/rdap-vs-whois): how expiry dates are read
- [Configuration](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/guide/configuration): environment variables and stored data

## Tools

- [Domain expiry checker](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/domain-expiry-checker/): RDAP lookup in the browser, with the TLDs that work

## Blog

- [All posts](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/blog/)
- [How to get a Slack webhook URL](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/blog/slack-webhook-url): Create a Slack incoming webhook, find the webhook URL, test it with curl and read Slack's error codes. Then paste it into Supadomain or Alertmanager.
- [Domain renewal: grace period, redemption and auto-renew](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/blog/domain-renewal): How domain renewal works for .com and other gTLDs under ICANN rules: reminder emails, auto-renew, the grace period after expiry, redemption fees and deletion.
- [Can you transfer a domain after it expires?](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/blog/transfer-expired-domain): Yes, in most cases. What ICANN's Transfer Policy says about expired domains, the 60-day locks, redemption, auth codes and the year a transfer adds.
- ["The RDAP server redacted the value": what it means](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/blog/rdap-server-redacted-the-value): Why RDAP lookups hide registrant names, emails and phone numbers, how RFC 9537 marks redacted fields, and which data stays visible, including expiry dates.
- [Domain expiry scam emails: check the real date first](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/blog/domain-expiry-scam-email): Got an urgent email saying your services may be interrupted due to domain expiry? How these scams work and how to check the real expiry date over RDAP.
- ["No registry RDAP server was identified": what it means](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/blog/no-registry-rdap-server): Why RDAP lookups fail for .io, .co, .de, .eu and 170 other ccTLDs, how the IANA bootstrap file works, and what to use for those domains instead.
- [How to check a domain expiry date without WHOIS](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/blog/check-domain-expiry-date): Check when a domain expires with an RDAP lookup: one curl command, a jq filter for the expiration event, days left in the shell, and the TLDs that hide it.
- [Expired domain names: what happens after deletion](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/blog/what-happens-to-expired-domains): The life of an expired domain name: the registrar's grace period, redemption, pending delete, release, drop catching, and what a new owner can do with it.
- [ICANN Lookup: what ICANN's registration data tool shows and where it gets it](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/blog/icann-lookup): ICANN Lookup is ICANN's RDAP client for domain data: what its results show, where each field comes from, why contacts are hidden, and the same query in curl.
- [Domain age: how to check when a domain was registered](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/blog/domain-age): Domain age is the time since a domain was registered. Read the registration date from RDAP with one command, and learn why transfers keep it but drops reset it.
- [A free WHOIS API: query RDAP and get JSON back](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/blog/whois-api): Use RDAP as a free WHOIS API: one HTTPS request returns JSON with expiry date, status, registrar and nameservers. Examples in curl and Node.js, plus the limits.
- [Domain status codes: clientTransferProhibited and the rest, explained](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/blog/domain-status-codes): What clientTransferProhibited, serverHold, redemptionPeriod and other domain status codes mean, who sets them, how RDAP shows them and when to act.
- [EPP code: the domain transfer code explained](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/blog/epp-code): An EPP code, or auth code, proves you hold a domain when you move it to a new registrar. Where to find it, ICANN's five-day rule and the lock to lift first.
- [Run MongoDB in Docker for a self-hosted app](https://projects.halit.org/supadomain/blog/mongodb-docker): Run MongoDB in Docker for a self-hosted app: a compose file with a root user, a named volume and a healthcheck, the authSource connection string and backups.
